decisions.rationale: Friedreich ataxia is a single named disease with one specific definition, so it is a Specific Disease mention in the title.

Frataxin deficiency is stated to be the primary cause of Friedreich ataxia. The 'deficiency' is qualified by a specific gene product, analogous to 'C7 deficiency' which the guidelines treat as a Specific Disease, so it is not a bare general term.

decisions.rationale: FRDA is the abbreviation for Friedreich ataxia and is annotated as its own separate mention, per the synonym rule.

decisions.rationale: The phrase describes a family of diseases (autosomal recessive cardiodegenerative and neurodegenerative diseases) rather than one specific disease, so it is a Disease Class. The conjoined adjectives modify one disease category and do not name two separate diseases, so it is not a Composite Mention.
